textos.A divisão sobre o filme gira em torno de: The divide over the film revolves around how the narrative and social issues are handled. textos.As reviews positivas frequentemente dest: Positive reviews frequently highlight how the film portrays violence and poverty in the favelas in a raw, realistic way, conveying a sense of authenticity that hits the viewer.
textos.Os elogios se concentram na fotografia m: The praise centers on the striking cinematography, the dynamic camera angles and the assured direction, which create an immersive, stylistically impressive visual experience.

textos.Dirigido por Fernando Meirelles e lançad: Directed by Fernando Meirelles and released in 2002, City of God is a Brazilian crime drama running 130 minutes. The plot follows Buscapé, a young man who grows up in a setting marked by urban crime and looks to photography as a path to building a different life.
textos.A obra se estrutura por meio de uma narr: The work is structured around a fragmented, nonlinear narrative, accompanied by a fast editing pace and a raw setting centered on violence and the daily life of the community.
textos.Na grande maioria das notas (~96%), boa: Among the vast majority of ratings (~96%), a good portion highlights the realistic, direct depiction of brutality as one of the central points of the work. In addition, several point to the cinematography and directing style as striking elements in the visual handling, while a portion value the screenplay's structure and the interweaving of the stories presented.
textos.Em contrapartida, para quem se posiciona: By contrast, for those in a minimal fraction of ratings (~3%), a considerable number feel that the constant intensity of the violence lessens the dramatic weight of the situations. From this perspective, a significant share argues that the production's technical polish creates an emotional distance from the events, and some report difficulty following the episodic chaining of the plot.
textos.Por fim, segundo a visão expressa numa f: Finally, according to the view expressed in an even smaller fraction of ratings (~1%), many see an exploitative, sensationalist tone in the treatment of the social setting.
